body:
## Summary

With `core.quotePath=true` (the loader's established pin, unchanged here) git quotes each `diff --git` header path **independently**. An ASCII-to-Unicode rename therefore arrives as:

```text
diff --git a/src/lib.rs "b/src/日本語.rs"
```

`parse_git_old_path` only recognized the unquoted ` b/` boundary, so for this asymmetric header it returned no old path. The exact rename-pair match in `handle_rename_metadata` then failed, `current_path` was cleared, and the renamed file silently vanished from scope: zero probes, zero findings, no rename notice, while a separately parseable section (the `Cargo.toml` `[lib]` path edit the fixture needs to stay valid) masked the missing scope with a complete-looking result. An isolated pure-rename section was refused as `malformed_diff`.

The fix is confined to the production old-path reader: it recognizes the independently quoted destination boundary (` "b/`) before its existing unquoted boundary. An unquoted old path cannot contain a quote — git would have C-quoted the whole path — so the quoted boundary is unambiguous. All existing metadata/disclosure consumers, the native decoder/confinement, the exact rename-from match, and the loader quoting pin are reused unchanged.

Distinct from the delivered ordinary-rename claim (#2668 / merged #2727): this is the asymmetric-header witness those controls did not cover.

## Acceptance predicates and red→green evidence

Red was captured with the tests committed against the unmodified reader; the same tests are green with the fix. Local runs: Windows, Rust 1.95.0.

1. **Literal, native-inventory controls cover all four old/new quoting combinations, pure and edited.**
   `path.rs::tests::parse_git_old_path_pairs_each_destination_quoting_layout` pins all four header layouts (both unquoted incl. spaces, old-quoted-only, new-quoted-only, both-quoted) plus the mixed-layout confinement rejection. Red: the new-quoted-only case returned `None` (`left: None`); green: all five assertions pass. The CLI matrix `mixed_quote_rename.rs::all_quoting_layouts_disclose_renames_pure_and_edited` builds **real git fixtures** for five layouts × pure/edited; every expected filename is pinned against `git diff --name-status -z` NUL inventory bytes, never derived from ripr's parser. Red: matrix failed at `new-quoted-only/pure`; green: all 10 arms pass.

2. **A pure mixed-quote rename is counted/disclosed without invented probes or a malformed-diff accusation; an adjacent parseable file cannot conceal it.**
   Red (CLI witness, matching the issue's executed numbers): `changed_file_count 1, changed_line_count 2` — only the Cargo.toml edit; zero probes/findings; no rename notice; the rename lost while the parseable neighbor survived. Green: `changed_file_count 2`, the pure-rename disclosure (`detected 1 pure rename(s) with no changed lines; rename-only changes produce no probes.`) is on stderr, `probes == 0`, no zero-scope/non-source disclosures, and `limitations` is empty. `mixed_quote_rename.rs::isolated_mixed_quote_pure_rename_section_is_disclosed_not_malformed` additionally isolates the quoted pure-rename section through the `--diff` route: red it was refused; green it exits 0 with the disclosure and no `malformed_diff` limitation. Parser units: `parse.rs::tests::metadata_registers_mixed_quote_pure_rename_under_new_path` (red `renamed_file_count 0` → green 1, `pure_rename_paths == [src/日本語.rs]`, no limitations, not truncated).

3. **Edited mixed-quote findings retain the new path, line 2, actual live/committed expression and the existing old-path-association limitation.**
   Red: `metadata_registers_mixed_quote_edited_rename_under_new_path` and the edited CLI arms failed pre-fix. Green: the parser unit pins the changed file at `src/日本語.rs`, line 2, added text `amount > threshold`; the CLI arm pins the predicate finding at `./<NUL-inventory new path>`, line 2, expression `amount > threshold`, plus the edited-rename disclosure (`old-path test associations are not carried forward`) on stderr.

4. **Existing confinement/adversarial path controls remain fail-closed.** No `core.quotePath=true` removal, no golden relabeling (no goldens touched). `cargo test -p ripr --lib analysis::diff`: 225 passed / 0 failed post-fix (222 pre-existing passed pre-fix); `cargo test -p ripr --lib rename`: 50 passed / 0 failed. The mixed-layout traversal control in the new unit test is rejected (`None`).

5. **Pre-repair red, candidate green, review, hosted CI.** Red→green captured locally per above; this PR carries the hosted proof (routed gate below) and independent exact-head review per the normal lane process.

## Non-goals (unchanged)

Test-association transfer, parser architecture, Python/TypeScript oracles, gate/policy/MCP/SDLC changes, releases. The inherited residual from the issue — a both-unquoted real-git old name containing ` b/` still splits at the first fallback delimiter — is deliberately out of scope and unchanged.

## Local verification

- `cargo test -p ripr --lib analysis::diff` — 225 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p ripr --lib rename` — 50 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p ripr --test cli_smoke mixed_quote_rename` — 3 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p ripr --lib --tests -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- `cargo xtask check-changelog-fragments` — pass
- `cargo xtask check-traceability` — pass (new tests linked under RIPR-SPEC-0170)

Closes #7795

reviews.body:
## Decision

- Needs reviewer attention before upstream: findings remain.

## Confirmed findings

- Siblings not enumerated exhaustively: cli_smoke module inclusion order (mixed_quote_rename placed before native_fanout) and any future sibling test module following the same shape should follow the same lang-rust gate pattern; this is calibration guidance, not a defect.

## Refuted

- split_once(" \"b/") could mis-split an unquoted old path containing literal space-quote-b inside it.; refuted because: Git would have whole-path C-quoted any path containing "; an unquoted old path cannot legitimately contain "; the new boundary is unambiguous and the unquoted split_once(" b/") fallback is retained for the unquoted-both case.
- A symmetric independently-quoted SOURCE boundary (vs the fixed DESTINATION boundary) creates a parallel blind spot in parse_new_path_marker or hunk readers.; refuted because: parse_new_path_marker and parse_diff_path_token operate on a single token and never split on ` b/`; hunk headers route through the same per-token decoder, so no analogous unquoted/quoted boundary exists to miss.

## Parked follow-ups

- Park for follow-up (not this PR): verify no other diff consumer assumes symmetric `a/... b/...` quoting outside path.rs; the inheritance list in the changelog fragment is currently scoped to metadata/disclosure/native decoder/confinement/loader pin only.

## Evidence gaps

- Model proof intent was rejected by deterministic validation.
